title: Self-Hosted Model Security Boundary
summary: Define and test artifact, caller, operator, network, secret, resource-abuse, audit, revocation, and recovery controls for a model service.
prerequisites: A complete serving-unit and trust-boundary diagram
Named human, workload, deployment, secret, network, and audit owners
Data classification, threat model, incident path, and recovery objectives

sections.title: Separate principals, authority, and paths
paragraphs: Name human users, applications, gateways, model workers, tools, deployment automation, administrators, and reviewers as separate principals. Authenticate at the boundary where a decision is enforced, authorize the specific action and resource, and propagate only the minimum identity context needed downstream. Prompt text, a model claim, a network location, or possession of a public endpoint is never proof of authority.

Separate inference, health, readiness, metrics, debugging, deployment, secret, model-download, and control-plane paths. Restrict ingress and egress to declared dependencies; protect local sockets and container or cluster control planes; remove unnecessary capabilities, devices, mounts, and privileges; and reject artifacts that lack immutable identity, license disposition, provenance, or integrity evidence.

sections.title: Control secrets, sensitive data, and resource abuse
paragraphs: Reference secrets from an external secret system or protected runtime boundary, scope them to one workload, rotate and revoke them, and prevent them from entering images, repositories, prompts, outputs, traces, screenshots, or learner evidence. Define allowlisted telemetry fields, redaction, bounded identifiers, access, retention, export, deletion, and a response for accidental collection.

Enforce request body, context, output, concurrency, rate, queue, deadline, retry, tool, and cost limits before scarce inference resources. Test missing, expired, forged, wrong-audience, wrong-role, revoked, cross-tenant, malformed, oversized, slow, replayed, and denied-egress cases. Audit policy decisions and consequential changes without turning the audit log into a copy of sensitive content.

Audit and data: [DECISIONS/EVENTS, REDACTION, ACCESS, RETENTION, EXPORT, DELETION, AND TAMPER EVIDENCE]

Stop conditions: [UNVERIFIED ARTIFACT, PRIVILEGE/CONTROL-PLANE EXPOSURE, SECRET/DATA LEAK, AUTHZ BYPASS, UNBOUNDED ABUSE, OR AUDIT LOSS]
Recovery: [DENY/ISOLATE, REVOKE/ROTATE, RECONCILE EFFECTS, REMOVE EXPOSED DATA UNDER POLICY, RESTORE VERIFIED POLICY AND BUILD]

sections.title: Expected evidence and verification
paragraphs: Expected evidence includes the serving-unit identity, trust boundaries, principals and permission matrix, negative authentication and authorization fixtures, network and egress tests, secret lifecycle, artifact verification, abuse limits, audit events, data controls, revocation, containment, recovery, owners, and dated residual risks. Security review covers the gateway, runtime, host or cluster, model files, tools, and management plane together.

Stop service or the narrow affected capability on authorization bypass, unverified artifact, exposed control plane, secret or protected-data disclosure, uncontrolled external effect, unbounded resource abuse, or missing required audit. Deny and isolate first, revoke and rotate affected credentials, reconcile uncertain effects before retry, remove exposed data under policy, restore the verified build and policy, and rerun negative cases before reopening.

sections.title: Supplemental v2: scope, transfer, and authoritative sources
paragraphs: Append this supplement without replacing or editing the original sections separate-principals-and-paths, control-data-secrets-and-abuse, and verify-security. It retains their scope across artifacts, human and workload principals, inference and management paths, hosts, containers or clusters, networks, egress, secrets, data, tools, audit, abuse controls, revocation, containment, and recovery.

The runnable example is deliberately limited. X-Classroom-Identity selects a synthetic in-memory classroom fixture. It is never production JWT verification and does not validate a cryptographic signature, issuer key, or production credential. Python http.server is also not recommended for production use because it implements only basic security checks. See the Python 3.11 HTTP server documentation, checked 2026-09-20: https://docs.python.org/3.11/library/http.server.html.

The server binds only its owned listener to 127.0.0.1 on an operating-system-assigned port, uses ThreadingHTTPServer so simultaneous backend calls can be tested, and closes that listener during teardown. BaseHTTPRequestHandler has already parsed the request line and headers before do_POST runs. The handler then calls socket.settimeout on the accepted connection before reading the declared body. This is a per-connection body inactivity timeout for the subsequent body read, not a total request deadline and not protection against slow or incomplete headers. Client requests separately use urllib.request timeouts. Relevant Python documentation, checked 2026-09-20: https://docs.python.org/3.11/library/http.server.html#http.server.ThreadingHTTPServer, https://docs.python.org/3.11/library/http.server.html#http.server.BaseHTTPRequestHandler, https://docs.python.org/3.11/library/socket.html#socket.socket.settimeout, and https://docs.python.org/3.11/library/urllib.request.html#urllib.request.urlopen.

The example uses unittest.TestCase, threading.BoundedSemaphore, time-like injectable clocks, JSONDecodeError handling, SHA-256, and constant-time digest comparison. Primary documentation, checked 2026-09-20: https://docs.python.org/3.11/library/unittest.html#unittest.TestCase, https://docs.python.org/3.11/library/threading.html#threading.BoundedSemaphore, https://docs.python.org/3.11/library/time.html#time.monotonic, https://docs.python.org/3.11/library/json.html#json.JSONDecodeError, https://docs.python.org/3.11/library/hashlib.html#hashlib.sha256, and https://docs.python.org/3.11/library/hmac.html#hmac.compare_digest.

Deny-by-default authorization is an application control, not proof of network isolation. The policy allows only declared role, path, action, resource, and tenant tuples. Deployment infrastructure must independently enforce ingress, egress, control-plane, and metadata-service restrictions. In the OWASP API Security Top 10 for 2023, API8 is Security Misconfiguration: https://owasp.github.io/API-Security/editions/2023/en/0x11-t10/. API9 is Improper Inventory Management, including problems with API and host inventory: https://owasp.github.io/API-Security/editions/2023/en/0x11-t09/. Broader operational references include Docker Engine security at https://docs.docker.com/engine/security/, NIST Cybersecurity Framework at https://www.nist.gov/cyberframework, and SLSA provenance 1.2 at https://slsa.dev/spec/v1.2/provenance. These URLs were checked in the supplied research on 2026-09-20.

The boundary method transfers to deployments containing Meta, Qwen, Microsoft Phi, Mistral, DeepSeek, Z.ai, or NVIDIA components because it evaluates the serving system rather than assuming a provider-specific security property. This statement makes no claim about any named model's capability, license, availability, safety, or deployment support. Those questions require dated first-party documentation for the exact selected artifact.

sections.title: Supplemental v2: concrete classroom control record
paragraphs: Protected outcome: only a valid tenant-a caller may invoke action call on resource model-a through /inference, and only a valid tenant-a operator may invoke action manage on resource gateway through /management. Missing, unrecognized, forged, revoked, expired, wrong-audience, wrong-role, cross-tenant, wrong-action, and wrong-resource requests are denied before fake-backend dispatch.

Data controls: request bodies are limited to 256 raw bytes before reading; inference prompts are limited to 128 strict UTF-8 bytes after authorization and JSON parsing; a prompt containing an unpaired surrogate is rejected as malformed input; fake-backend output is reduced to at most 64 UTF-8 bytes; and JSON must be an object with correctly typed fields. These are separate limits. The bounded-body fixture measures the complete serialized request body before the server reads it, while the context check measures only the parsed prompt after encoding that string as UTF-8. Therefore a valid raw-UTF-8 request can be no larger than 256 bytes while its prompt is still more than 128 UTF-8 bytes. Audit events contain exactly decision, caller, action, resource, tenant, and reason. Every audit value is selected from a bounded allowlist. Caller values are recorded only after synthetic identity lookup, action and resource come from the recognized path rather than the payload, tenant comes from the validated identity fixture, and reason is an internal policy label. Unknown or out-of-domain values become fixed fallback labels, so raw headers, payload action, payload resource, payload tenant, prompts, and secrets are not copied into audit.

Abuse controls: an injectable monotonic clock enforces one accepted dispatch per synthetic identity per second without sleep-based test flakiness. A nonblocking BoundedSemaphore permits at most two backend calls in flight. The concurrency test uses events as barriers so two backend calls are known to be occupied before a third request is sent. After the HTTP request line and headers have already been parsed, the handler applies a one-second timeout to the accepted connection for the body read. If the declared body remains incomplete without further data until that read times out, the fixture returns HTTP 408. This is a body inactivity timeout, not a total request deadline or header timeout. The client timeout is two seconds for ordinary urllib requests.

Dispatch witness: backend_calls changes only after authentication, authorization, schema, body, context, rate, and concurrency checks pass. Each denial test snapshots this counter and proves that its denial leaves the value unchanged. The permitted inference and management tests prove that the two paths have separate successful policies.

Artifact witness: the program computes a SHA-256 digest from local fixture bytes, verifies the original bytes with hmac.compare_digest, then verifies that altered bytes do not match. This is a concrete integrity demonstration, not provenance for a deployed image or model.

Inspection state before an independent run: EXPECTED, not PASS. The code and deterministic success transcript are supplied below, but this revision does not claim they have already been executed. Deployment state: HOLD. Publication, model review, or a successful localhost run cannot remove that HOLD.

sections.title: Supplemental v2: runnable Python 3.11+ gateway and unittest client
paragraphs: Prerequisites: Python 3.11 or newer and permission to open a localhost TCP listener. No external package, external network, model download, credential, private data, temporary directory, or pre-existing service is required.

Save the code exactly as security_gateway_v2.py. Run it from that directory with python3 security_gateway_v2.py. On Windows, use py -3.11 security_gateway_v2.py if that command selects Python 3.11 or newer.

A successful independent run prints exactly the transcript in the next section. The program suppresses unittest's duration-dependent normal report and emits a fixed success transcript only after all 18 unittest methods pass. On failure, it emits unittest diagnostic details instead and exits nonzero. Test 09 deliberately sends MAX_BODY + 1 raw bytes and stops at the pre-read body boundary. Test 12 deliberately sends a complete JSON body serialized with json.dumps(..., ensure_ascii=False), proves len(encoded_body) <= MAX_BODY and len(prompt.encode('utf-8')) > MAX_CONTEXT_BYTES, then exercises the separate post-parse context limit.

sections.title: Supplemental v2: pass/fail inspection and deployment HOLD
paragraphs: Code review record, dated 2026-09-20: the revised source contains executable checks for the declared inference and management permissions; revoked caller and operator fixtures; expired, forged, missing, wrong-audience, wrong-role, cross-tenant, wrong-action, and wrong-resource denials; malformed JSON, array, null, malformed field types, and a JSON-escaped lone-surrogate prompt; distinct raw-body and UTF-8-context limits; output, rate, concurrency, and post-header body-inactivity limits; bounded audit values that exclude raw action, resource, tenant, header, and prompt content; backend non-reachability on every tested denial; owned-server shutdown; and altered-artifact rejection. The socket test does not establish a total request deadline or header protection. Independent execution record supplied for the reviewed v4 correction: the initial Windows V3 run failed test12 with ConnectionAbortedError because the escaped prompt exceeded MAX_BODY and reached the 413 body boundary; after changing test12 to raw UTF-8 serialization and adding the explicit size assertions, the repeated Windows run passed all 18 top-level tests with the exact output below. The first failed run is retained as causal feedback, not as a passing result.

Deployment acceptance is HOLD because no deployment evidence accompanies this supplement. A local PASS would establish only the behavior of the classroom process on the machine where it ran. It would not establish production identity validation, network egress denial, host hardening, container isolation, secret lifecycle, deployed-byte provenance, telemetry retention, recovery readiness, or provider-specific suitability.

Fail the local inspection if any denial changes backend_calls; any attacker-controlled action, resource, tenant, identity header, prompt, or secret appears in audit; an array, null, or lone surrogate causes an uncaught handler exception; a wrong resource is accepted; more than two backend hooks enter simultaneously; a repeated identity dispatches before one injected second; the tested post-header inactive body lacks the 408 response; output exceeds 64 UTF-8 bytes; altered artifact bytes verify; or the owned listener remains running. Do not interpret the body-inactivity test as evidence of header protection or a total request deadline.

Fail or keep HOLD for the deployment if there is an authorization bypass, an unverified running artifact, an exposed management or control-plane path, a secret or protected-data disclosure, an undeclared external effect, unbounded resource use, missing required audit, or absent recovery evidence. Publication is never deployment acceptance.

sections.title: Supplemental v2: concrete deployment inspection procedures
paragraphs: Use only commands applicable to the deployment and run them under an approved change and evidence-collection process. Record command, timestamp, host or cluster identity, operator, exit status, and unredacted evidence location. Redact copies used for review without destroying the controlled original. Do not copy secret values into tickets, terminals captured by learners, or this lesson.

Host procedure: on each serving host, capture uname -a, cat /etc/os-release, id for the service account, ss -lntup or the platform equivalent, findmnt, systemctl cat SERVICE_NAME, systemctl show SERVICE_NAME -p User -p Group -p NoNewPrivileges -p PrivateTmp -p ProtectSystem -p ProtectHome -p CapabilityBoundingSet, and getcap -r / 2>/dev/null. Replace SERVICE_NAME only with the reviewed unit name. Compare listeners, users, groups, mounts, devices, capabilities, and unit restrictions with the approved trust-boundary diagram. HOLD for an unknown listener, root execution without written necessity, unexpected device or control socket, broad writable mount, missing patch record, or absent owner.

Container procedure for Docker where applicable: record docker image inspect IMAGE_REFERENCE --format '{{json .RepoDigests}}'; docker inspect CONTAINER_NAME --format '{{json .Config.User}} {{json .HostConfig.Privileged}} {{json .HostConfig.CapAdd}} {{json .HostConfig.Devices}} {{json .HostConfig.Binds}} {{json .HostConfig.ReadonlyRootfs}} {{json .HostConfig.NetworkMode}}'; and docker diff CONTAINER_NAME. Do not collect .Config.Env because it can expose secrets. Compare the observed immutable digest, user, privileges, capabilities, devices, mounts, root filesystem, network mode, and writable changes with approved configuration. HOLD for a mutable-only image reference, privileged mode, unexplained capability, host control socket, broad host mount, or secret embedded in an image layer.

Cluster procedure for Kubernetes where applicable: preserve kubectl get deployment DEPLOYMENT -n NAMESPACE -o yaml, kubectl get pod -n NAMESPACE -l APP_SELECTOR -o yaml, kubectl get networkpolicy -n NAMESPACE -o yaml, and kubectl auth can-i --as=system:serviceaccount:NAMESPACE:SERVICE_ACCOUNT --list -n NAMESPACE. Review image digests, securityContext, serviceAccountName, automountServiceAccountToken, volume and device access, host namespaces, admission results, and role bindings. Do not retrieve Secret values. HOLD for host networking or namespaces without necessity, privileged containers, unrestricted service-account authority, mutable-only images, absent applicable admission evidence, or unexplained control-plane access.

Network procedure: enumerate every inference, health, readiness, metrics, debug, deployment, secret, model-download, telemetry, DNS, proxy, metadata, and control-plane flow in a source-destination-port-purpose table. From a separate approved test workload in the same policy scope, connect to every declared destination and to controlled undeclared canary destinations on representative TCP and UDP paths. Preserve firewall, security-group, network-policy, service-mesh, DNS, and proxy decision logs. Verify that inference clients cannot reach management ports, workloads cannot reach the host or orchestration control socket, and undeclared egress and metadata endpoints are denied. Application HTTP denials do not satisfy this procedure. HOLD if a required deny test is absent or unexpectedly connects.

Secret procedure: create a metadata-only inventory containing secret reference, issuer, owner, consuming workload, scope, creation date, rotation requirement, last rotation, expiry, revocation path, and access-log location. Confirm deployment configuration references the secret system rather than containing a value. Inspect repository history, build context, image-layer scan reports, prompt and output stores, traces, screenshots, and exported evidence for accidental collection. Exercise revocation or rotation with a dedicated test credential, verify the old credential fails, verify the intended workload obtains the replacement, and preserve timestamps and audit events. Never print a real secret during verification. HOLD if ownership, rotation, revocation, or leakage-response evidence is absent.

Artifact procedure: record the exact model, tokenizer, adapter, runtime, gateway, policy, and image identifiers. Compute local digests with sha256sum FILE or the operating-system equivalent, compare them with approved immutable digests using a tool that returns nonzero on mismatch, verify available signatures and provenance under the organization's trust policy, document source and license disposition, and inspect the running process or container digest rather than only a registry tag. Preserve build identity and dependency records. SLSA provenance can contribute provenance evidence, but it does not by itself prove that running bytes match the reviewed artifact. HOLD on any mismatch or missing required provenance.

Audit and data procedure: generate one approved allow and each required denial, then query the production audit destination using the reviewer role. Confirm decision identifiers and bounded principal references are present while prompts, outputs, bearer credentials, secret values, and raw untrusted headers are absent. Inspect access control, retention, export, deletion, alerting, clock synchronization, and tamper evidence. Exercise the accidental-collection response with synthetic data. HOLD if policy decisions cannot be reconstructed or sensitive content is copied without an approved need and control.

Recovery procedure: conduct a dated exercise that introduces a synthetic authorization-policy fault or unavailable artifact in an isolated environment. Measure detection; deny or isolate the affected capability; revoke the test identity; rotate a test secret; reconcile uncertain external effects before retry; restore the approved digest and policy; verify backup or rollback integrity; and rerun authentication, authorization, egress, abuse, audit, revocation, and artifact negative tests. Record recovery objective, measured result, owner, approver, residual risk, and corrective actions. HOLD until the exercise succeeds or an authorized risk owner records a time-bounded exception.

sections.title: Supplemental v2: independent changed task
paragraphs: Changed task, presented before its answer: A synthetic identity named revoked-operator has role operator, tenant tenant-a, audience classroom-gateway, and a future expiry, but its revocation flag is true. It sends POST /management with action manage, resource gateway, and tenant tenant-a. Determine the HTTP status, whether the fake backend is reached, the audit reason, and whether its operator role can override revocation.

Executable verification requirement: save and run the reviewed v4 source. The independent changed case is test_07_changed_task_revoked_operator. Its success is represented by the exact line PASS 07 changed task revoked operator only after the complete unittest suite succeeds. The Windows repeated run supplied for this review produced that line and passed all 18 top-level tests.

sections.title: Supplemental v2: separate answer and causal feedback
paragraphs: Answer: return HTTP 401, do not reach the fake backend, record reason revoked using only the audit allowlist, and do not let the operator role override revocation.
Exact task result: decision=DENY; status=401; backend_reached=NO; audit_reason=revoked; role_overrides_revocation=NO.

Causal grading: if the learner returns 200 because the role, action, resource, and tenant match, the causal error is authorizing before applying revocation. If the learner returns 403, the request is still denied, but the classification misses the fixture's failed identity status, which this lab maps to 401 before role authorization. If backend_calls increases, the causal error is dispatching before the final identity and policy decision. If the raw header, prompt, or secret enters audit, the causal error is copying untrusted or sensitive input instead of recording bounded decision metadata. If the learner calls this production JWT verification, the causal error is confusing synthetic lookup with cryptographic authentication. If the learner accepts a deployment from this result, the causal error is confusing a local application-policy witness with deployment evidence for network, host, container, secrets, artifacts, audit operations, and recovery.

sections.title: Supplemental v2: assumptions
paragraphs: The original three sections supplied in the work item remain unchanged and these supplemental sections will be appended to them.
The independent runner has Python 3.11 or newer and can bind a loopback port. The lab does not assume Docker, Kubernetes, a model runtime, external network access, or production credentials.
The deployment inspection commands are conditional on the named platform. An approved platform-equivalent command may be used when it captures the same evidence.

sections.title: Supplemental v2: omitted items
paragraphs: The initial Windows V3 run failed test12 with ConnectionAbortedError and is not a pass. The corrected v4 source was independently rerun on Windows and passed all 18 top-level tests. No deployment execution or deployment evidence is claimed.

No deployment evidence was supplied, so production authentication, host, container or cluster, network, egress, secret, artifact provenance, audit operations, and recovery results remain HOLD rather than being invented.
No provider-specific license, model capability, availability, or security claim is made because no dated first-party source for a selected provider artifact was supplied.
